name: Palacio de Cibeles

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/16322055 (centroid of the outline; the main façade is the cut corner facing the Plaza de Cibeles, at 308.5°)

rights.note: Palacio de Comunicaciones, 1904–1919, by Antonio Palacios and Joaquín Otamendi (protected until 80 years after Otamendi's death); sculpture by Ángel García Díaz. Converted into the Madrid city hall and CentroCentro by Arquimática (2003–2011), with the glass roof over the old courtyard by Schlaich Bergermann und Partner (2008–2009).

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1849031_palacio_de_cibeles.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. Massing from the OpenStreetMap outline and its building:part ways (levels mapped to heights: 5 → 24 m, 6 → 27, 7 → 30.5, 8 → 33.5), with an 18 m base under everything; the rear range on the old Pasaje de Alarcón has no OSM part and is modelled as a 24 m block. Heights of the main façade, corner towers (36 m, crowns to about 46 m) and central tower (base 41 m, shaft to 58 m with clocks, lantern and finial to 70 m) measured on frontal photos (±5 %). Windows are dark panels in a regular rhythm (about 3.7 m bays), not the real bay layout; the plateresque ornament, balconies, galleries and sculpture are reduced to cornices, parapets, pinnacles and two stylised statues. Grey slate mansards are generic insets of each part; the glass vault over the old courtyard is a smooth cushion (the real one is a steel gridshell). Uncertain: the exact heights of the rear ranges and of the inner courts. footprint = the OSM outline grown by 1.5 m, so the forecourt on the Plaza de Cibeles is not cleared.
